solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: View old river in place of canal

indicators.note: the old river letters are placed inside the name of the canal's country

parts.note: Panama is the country that gives its name to the Panama Canal

explanation.surface: A sightseer surveys the landscape where a former river once ran instead of a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping scene, so it is a synonym for a view.

clue.text: Crop that's barely changed — just slightly

indicators.note: the letters of barely are altered only a little, since just two swap places

parts.note: taken as written, the word the clue says is changed

explanation.surface: A field of grain has barely altered, only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the E and L of barely trade places, which is why the change is 'just slight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley is a cereal grown as a farm crop.

clue.text: From what we hear, become more sunny in this English resort

indicators.note: signals that the answer is a word that sounds like the phrase that follows

parts.note: weather that brightens grows sunnier

explanation.surface: A weather forecast promises sunnier skies at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a famous seaside holiday town in Sussex, an example of an English resort.

clue.text: Second record is a big hit

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A second chart record turns out to be a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'big hit' suggest music charts; here a slog is a hard swipe of the ball, as in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog the ball is to strike it hard and wildly, so a slog is a big hit.

clue.text: Romans adjusted price of freedom

indicators.note: the letters of Romans are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans revised what a captive had to pay to be released.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the money demanded to release a captive, the cost of their liberty.

clue.text: You and I are — or used to be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the contraction ..., short for we are
second meaning: the past tense of are

explanation.walkthrough: The grid ignores the apostrophe, so WE'RE and the past tense look the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction for we are and the plural past tense of the verb be share the same letters.

clue.text: What's central in proclamation for holy man

indicators.note: the letters sitting in the very centre of the long word are taken, two either side of its midpoint

parts.note: the four-letter word sits at the centre of this twelve-letter word

explanation.surface: A decree is issued on behalf of a religious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a holy man.

clue.text: Let out — or let out again?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., rented out once more

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RE-LEASED and it means a property rented out a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means freed, and split as re-leased it means rented to a tenant once more.

clue.text: Follow part of journey, arriving at sharp bend

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a leg is one stage of a trip

explanation.surface: A driver tails another car on one stage of a trip and reaches a hairpin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a road or golf hole with an abrupt angle, a sharp turn.

clue.text: Mark, for example, what's indubitably true

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Mark's is one of the four ...
second meaning: ... truth, something beyond doubt

explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name or a score, but it is the evangelist whose book is a Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Each New Testament account of Christ is a Gospel, and taking something as gospel means treating it as certain fact.

clue.text: Curling and very short in style

indicators.note: the short letter sits inside the word for style

parts.note: a way of doing something is its style or manner
very shortened to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Hair is curled and cut very short in a fashionable style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curling' suggests the sport on ice, but here it describes hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavy hair is hair that curls in undulations, so it describes something curling.

clue.text: Varieties of meat for someone on one's side

indicators.note: plural varieties means more than one rearrangement of the letters of meat, here two side by side

parts.note: the word is taken twice over, since plural varieties asks for two separate rearrangements of it

explanation.surface: A butcher's selection of meats is offered to a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The word meat is rearranged twice, as TEAM and as MATE, and the two varieties are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate is a fellow member of a sports team, a person playing for the same side.

clue.text: Move right into passage for story with moral

indicators.note: the letters for move and right go inside the passage

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage between buildings
to go is to move

explanation.surface: An instruction to step right into a corridor, then tell a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a tale whose characters stand for ideas, carrying a moral or lesson.

clue.text: Altering in new arrangement for percussion instrument

indicators.note: the letters of altering are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A band changes the arrangement of a piece to feature a percussion part.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a steel bar bent into three sides, struck with a beater in an orchestra.

clue.text: Borderline that's awfully alarming

indicators.note: the letters of alarming are awfully jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something only just acceptable is described as dreadfully worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal case is one at the edge, so it is a synonym of borderline.

clue.text: Information about antique, kind of mean

indicators.note: the word for information is wrapped about the word for antique

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
something antique is old

explanation.surface: Facts about an antique piece reveal it is somewhat stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests miserliness; it is the mathematical or philosophical mean, as in the golden mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden mean is a moderate middle course, or the golden ratio, one type of mean.

clue.text: Wife accompanying that fellow? Fancy that

parts.note: him refers to a man already mentioned

explanation.surface: A wife going along with her husband, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden impulse or passing desire, a fancy.

clue.text: Altogether saintlike pronouncement

indicators.note: the answer is what the word for saintlike sounds like when pronounced

parts.note: saints are holy

explanation.surface: A wholly pious declaration from a saintly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly means completely or entirely, a synonym of altogether.

clue.text: Everything put into naughty traditional song

indicators.note: the word for everything goes inside the word for naughty

parts.note: a naughty child is bad
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything is crammed into a cheeky old folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or poem passed down in folk tradition.

clue.text: Terse reassurance from me that's run by people in frenzy

definitions.text: that's run by people in frenzy

parts.note: what I say about myself: the first-person verb, as in I am
a two-letter word saying all is fine

explanation.surface: A curt 'I'm fine' from someone as a crowd runs wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I AM OK' minus the I. To run amok is the fixed phrase, so the definition is what people run when they are in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amok means in a wild uncontrolled state, as in the idiom run amok.

clue.text: Like enthusiast, turning up for such a temperamental singer

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is turned upward, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: an enthusiast is avid, keen on their interest, so this is the adjective for being like one

explanation.surface: A keen fan arrives to see a moody opera star.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, often with a reputation for being difficult.

clue.text: Pulverized earth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crushed into powder, the past of grind

explanation.definitionFit: Ground is the past participle of grind, meaning crushed fine, and it is also the soil or land surface.

clue.text: Confused Romeo and half of Verona also

indicators.note: the letters of Romeo are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: A muddled Romeo, and part of Verona too, from Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover means in addition, besides, so it is a synonym for also.

clue.text: Quiet spell university had in fifties

indicators.note: the fifties hold the university letter inside them

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, and several fifties give a row of them

explanation.surface: A calm period at college during the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifties' suggests the decade; it is a string of Roman numeral fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull is a temporary period of calm or inactivity.
